1922.subject: Zoology
1922.text:
A small rise in the body temperature of humans is corrected by
(i) sweating
(ii) dilating the skin arteries
(iii) constricting the skin arteries
(iv) increased tension of muscles in the skin.
1922.sol:
A small rise in body temperature is detected by sensory receptors in the skin and by special neurons, which monitor blood temperature, in the hypothalamus itself. When the neural centre of the hypothalamus involved in lowering body temperature receives information that body temperature is too high, it commands the arteries of the skin to dilate so that more blood, and therefore more heat, reaches the surface where heat can be lost.
A large rise in body temperature causes the hypothalamus to command both an extreme dilation in the arteries of the skin and the release of sweat from the body.

2161.subject: Zoology
2161.text: During protein synthesis in an organism at one point the process comes to a halt. Select the group of the three codons from the following, from which any one of the three could bring about this halt.
2161.sol:
Non sense codon or terminator codon are the codons that do not code for any amino acid. It is a set of three nucleotides for which there is no corresponding tRNA molecule to insert an amino acid into the polypeptide chain. Protein synthesis is hence terminated and the completed polypeptide released from the ribosome. Three stop codons are UAA (ochre), UAG (amber) and UGA (opal).
Mutations which generate any of these three codons in a position which normally contains a codon specifying an amino acid are known as nonsense mutations.

2211.subject: Zoology
2211.text: Which of the following associations shows mutualism?
2211.sol: Mutualism is an interaction between two organisms of different species in which both the partners are benefitted, with none of the two capable of living separately. In many species of fig trees there is a relationship with the pollinator species of wasp. The female wasp uses the fruit not only as an oviposition site but uses the developing seeds within the fruit for nourishing its larvae. The wasp pollinates the fig inflorescence, while searching for suitable egg-laying sites. The fig returns this favour of pollination by offering the wasp some of its developing seeds, as food for the developing wasp larvae.

3334.subject: Chemistry
3334.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
3334.text: In which of the following options order of arrangement does not agree with the variation of property indicated against it?
3334.sol:
Electron gain enthalpy becomes less negative on moving down a group due to increase in atomic size. However, the electron gain enthalpy of $\mathrm{F}$ is less negative than $\mathrm{CI}$ due to electron-electron repulsion in small-sized $\mathrm{F}$ atom. Thus, the correct order is $\mathrm{F} < \mathrm{CI} > \mathrm{Br} > \mathrm{l}$.
$\mathrm{F}, \mathrm{CI}, \mathrm{Br}$ and $\mathrm{I}$ have $\Delta e_g H$ values (in $\mathrm{kJ}^{\mathrm{Jmol}} \mathrm{I}^{-1}$ )
$-328,-349,-325$ and -295 respectively. That order of arrangement does not agree with the variation of property.
Hence, the correct option is (3).

3348.subject: Chemistry
3348.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
3348.text:
Identify the correct statements from the following :
I. Tendency to form halide hydrates gradually increases from Be to Ba down the group.
II. Tendency to form stable super oxides increases from \($\mathrm{Li}$\) to \($\mathrm{Cs}$\) down the group.
III. Low solubility of \($\mathrm{LiF}$\) is due to its high lattice energy.
IV. Solubility of carbonates of group-2 elements increases down the group.
3348.sol:
(II) On moving down in the group the size of the atom increases. The positive charge around the ion gets weaken. The bigger atom can stabilise the bigger superoxide ion with less negative field.
(III) Due to smaller size of \(\mathrm{F}^{-}\)ion, the lattice energy increases. While, hydration enthalpy is less than that of lattice energy. Hence, LiF has very low solubility.
Statements (II, III) are correct.
Thus, correct option is (c).

9025.text: Let origin be the centre, $\left(\pm 3, 0\right)$ be the foci and $\dfrac{3}{2}$ be the eccentricity of a hyperbola. Then the line $2x - y - 1 = 0$
options: intersects the hyperbola at two points
passes through the vertex of the hyperbola
9025.sol:
Given,

Origin be the centre, $\left(\pm 3, 0\right)$ be the foci and $\dfrac{3}{2}$ be the eccentricity of a hyperbola,

Now we know that foci is& $\left(\pm ae, 0\right) ≡ \left(\pm3, 0\right)$,

So $ae = 3$ and given& $e = \dfrac{3}{2}$$ then& $a = $\dfrac{1}{2}$$,$$

Now by formula $b^{2} = a^{2} $\left(e^{2} - 1\right)$$ we get& $b = $\dfrac{5}{4}$$

So, equation of hyperbola will be \dfrac{x2}{\dfrac{1}{4}} - \dfrac{y2}{\dfrac{5}{16}} =1$

$⇒ 20x^{2} - y^{2} = 80$

Now putting the value of $y$ from the& line $2x - y - 1 = 0$ in hyperbola to check intersecting or not,

So,& $20x^{2} - \left(2x - 1\right)2 = 80$

$⇒ 16x^{2} + 4x - 81 = 0$

Now discriminant $D = {4}^{2} + 4 \times16 \times81 > 0$, hence line does not intersect the hyperbola.

12244.text:
The point $(3,2)$ undergoes the following three transformations in the order given
(i) Reflection about the line $y=x$.
(ii) Translation by the distance 1 unit in the positive direction of $x$-axis.
(iii) Rotation by an angle $\frac{\pi}{4}$ about the origin in the anti-clockwise direction.

12244.sol:
Given point is $(3,2)$.
(i) Reflection of point $(3,2)$ about the line $y=x$ is $(2,3)$.
(ii) Translation of a point through 1 unit distance in the positive direction of $x$-axis is $(3,3)$.
(iii)
$\begin{aligned} X & =-x \cos \theta+y \sin \theta \\ & =\left(-\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}\right)=0\end{aligned}$ and $Y=x \sin \theta+y \cos \theta=\left(\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}\right)=3 \sqrt{2}=\sqrt{18}$
Hence, final position is $(0, \sqrt{18})$.

12579.text: The cartesian equation of the plane whose vector equation is $\gamma=(1+\lambda-\mu) \hat{\mathbf{i}}+(2-\lambda) \hat{\mathbf{j}}+(3-2 \lambda+2 \mu) \hat{\mathbf{k}}$ where $\lambda, \mu$ are scalars, is
12579.sol:
$\begin{aligned}
& \gamma=(1+\lambda-\mu) \hat{i}+(2-\lambda) \hat{j}+(3-2 \lambda+2 \mu) \hat{k} \\
& =\hat{i}+\lambda \hat{i}-\mu \hat{i}+2 \hat{j}-\lambda \hat{j}+3 \hat{k}-2 \lambda \hat{k}+2 \mu \hat{k} \\
& =(\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+3 \hat{k})+\lambda(\hat{i}-\hat{j}-2 \hat{k})+\mu(-\hat{i}+2 \hat{k})
\end{aligned}$
Equation of plane is given by
$\{r-(\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+3 \hat{k})\}+[(\hat{i}-\hat{j}-2 \hat{k}) \times(-\hat{i}+2 \hat{k})]=0\begin{array}{ll}
\Rightarrow & \{r-(\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+3 \hat{k})\} \cdot(-2 \hat{i}-\hat{k})=0 \\
\Rightarrow & r(2 \hat{i}+\hat{k})-5=0 \\
\Rightarrow & r(2 \hat{i}+\hat{k})=5
\end{array}
Now, equation of plane in cartesian form
\begin{aligned}
& (x \hat{i}+y \hat{j}+z \hat{k}) \cdot(2 \hat{j}+\hat{k})=5 \\
& \therefore \quad 2 x+z=5
\end{aligned}$

\(\begin{aligned}$\frac{1}{L^{\prime}}$& =$\frac{1}{L_1}$+$\frac{1}{L_2}+$\frac{1}{L_3}$+$\frac{1}{L_4}\\
& =$\frac{1}{L / 4}$+$\frac{1}{L / 4$}+$\frac{1}{L / 4}+$\frac{1}{L / 4}$\\
& $=\frac{4}{L}+\frac{4}{L}+\frac{4}{L}+\frac{4}{L}\\
\Rightarrow $\frac{1}{L^{\prime}}$& =$\frac{16}{L}\Rightarrow$L^{\prime}=\frac{L}{16}
\end{aligned}\)

& =\frac{3}{4} \cdot \frac{g R^2 \cdot m}{R} \quad\left[\because G M=g R²\right] \\
& =\frac{3}{4} m g R
\end{aligned}
$

19835.text: For the equilibrium, $2 \mathrm{NOCl}(g) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{NO}(g)+\mathrm{Cl}_{2}(g)$, the value of the equilibrium constant, $K_{C}$ is $3.75 \times 10^{-6}$ at $1069 \mathrm{ K}$. The value of $K_{p}$ for the reaction at this temperature will be
19835.sol:
The relationship between the equilibrium constants $K_{p}$ and $K_{c}$ is given by the equation $K_{p} = K_{c}(RT)^{\Delta n_{g}}$.

For the reaction $2 \mathrm{NOCl}(g) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{NO}(g) + \mathrm{Cl}_{2}(g)$, the change in the number of moles of gaseous species is calculated as $\Delta n_{g} = (2 + 1) - 2 = 1$.

Given values are $K_{c} = 3.75 \times 10^{-6}$, $R = 0.0821 \text{ L atm K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$, and $T = 1069 \text{ K}$.

Substituting these values into the formula:

$K_{p} = (3.75 \times 10^{-6}) \times (0.0821 \times 1069)^{1}$

$K_{p} = 3.75 \times 10^{-6} \times 87.7649$

$K_{p} \approx 0.000329118$

Rounding to the appropriate precision, $K_{p} \approx 0.00033$.

Answer: $0.00033$

20461.subject: Chemistry
20461.text: What would be the volume of water required to dissolve $0.2 \mathrm{ g}$ of $\mathrm{PbCl}_2$ of molar mass $278 \mathrm{ g} / \mathrm{mol}$ to prepare a saturated solution of the salt? $(\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{SP}}$ of $\mathrm{PbCl}_2=3.2 \times 10^{-8})$
20461.sol:
The solubility equilibrium for $\text{PbCl}_{2}$ is given by $\text{PbCl}_{2}(s) \rightleftharpoons \text{Pb}^{2+}(aq) + 2\text{Cl}^{-}(aq)$.

Let $s$ be the solubility of $\text{PbCl}_{2}$ in mol/L. Then $[\text{Pb}^{2+}] = s$ and $[\text{Cl}^{-}] = 2s$.

The solubility product constant is $K_{sp} = [\text{Pb}^{2+}][\text{Cl}^{-}]^{2} = s(2s)^{2} = 4s^{3}$.

Given $K_{sp} = 3.2 \times 10^{-8}$, we have $4s^{3} = 3.2 \times 10^{-8} \Rightarrow s^{3} = 0.8 \times 10^{-8} = 8 \times 10^{-9}$.

Taking the cube root, $s = 2 \times 10^{-3} \text{ mol/L}$.

The number of moles of $\text{PbCl}_{2}$ in $0.2 \text{ g}$ is $n = \dfrac{0.2 \text{ g}}{278 \text{ g/mol}} \approx 7.194 \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol}$.

The volume $V$ required to dissolve this amount is $V = \dfrac{n}{s} = \dfrac{7.194 \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol}}{2 \times 10^{-3} \text{ mol/L}} = 0.3597 \text{ L}$.

Converting to milliliters, $V = 0.3597 \times 1000 \text{ ml} = 359.7 \text{ ml}$.

Answer: 359.7 ml

20640.subject: Chemistry
20640.text: The mole fraction of an unknown solute in 1560 g of Benzene is 0.5. What is the molality of the solution? (M. M of Benzene:78 amu)
20640.sol:
Let $n_B$ be the number of moles of Benzene and $n_S$ be the number of moles of solute.

The mass of Benzene is $1560$ g and its molar mass is $78$ g/mol. Thus, $n_B = \dfrac{1560}{78} = 20$ moles.

The mole fraction of the solute is given as $x_S = 0.5$. Since $x_S + x_B = 1$, the mole fraction of Benzene is $x_B = 1 - 0.5 = 0.5$.

The relationship between mole fractions is $\dfrac{n_S}{n_B} = \dfrac{x_S}{x_B} = \dfrac{0.5}{0.5} = 1$.

Therefore, $n_S = n_B = 20$ moles.

Molality $m$ is defined as the number of moles of solute per kilogram of solvent. The mass of the solvent (Benzene) is $1560$ g, which is $1.56$ kg.

$m = \dfrac{n_S}{\text{mass of solvent in kg}} = \dfrac{20}{1.56} \approx 12.82$ mol/kg.

Answer: $12.8$

21001.text: The area of the region in the first quadrant enclosed by the $x$-axis, the line $x = \sqrt{3}\,y$ and the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 4$ is
21001.sol:
The given circle is $x^2 + y^2 = 4$, which has its center at the origin $(0,0)$ and radius $r = 2$.

The given line is $x = \sqrt{3}y$, which can be rewritten as $y = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}x$.

The angle made by this line with the positive $x$-axis is $\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

The required region in the first quadrant is a sector of the circle bounded by the $x$-axis ($\theta = 0$) and the line ($\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$).

The area of a circular sector is given by $\dfrac{1}{2} r^2 \theta$.

Area $= \dfrac{1}{2} \times (2)^2 \times \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ sq units.

Alternatively, using integration by finding the intersection point $(\sqrt{3}, 1)$:

Area $= \int_{0}^{\sqrt{3}} \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{3}} dx + \int_{\sqrt{3}}^{2} \sqrt{4 - x^2} dx$

Area $= \left[ \dfrac{x^2}{2\sqrt{3}} \right]_{0}^{\sqrt{3}} + \left[ \dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{4-x^2} + 2\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) \right]_{\sqrt{3}}^{2}$

Area $= \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \left( \pi - \left( \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \dfrac{2\pi}{3} \right) \right) = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ sq units.

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{3}\ sq\ units$

21649.text: If $\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \dfrac{x^4-1}{x-1}=\lim _{x \rightarrow k} \dfrac{x^3-k^3}{x^2-k^2}$, then the value of K is
21649.sol:
Evaluate the first limit:
$\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \dfrac{x^4-1}{x-1} = \lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \dfrac{(x-1)(x^3+x^2+x+1)}{x-1} = \lim _{x \rightarrow 1} (x^3+x^2+x+1) = 1+1+1+1 = 4$.

Evaluate the second limit:
$\lim _{x \rightarrow k} \dfrac{x^3-k^3}{x^2-k^2} = \lim _{x \rightarrow k} \dfrac{(x-k)(x^2+xk+k^2)}{(x-k)(x+k)} = \lim _{x \rightarrow k} \dfrac{x^2+xk+k^2}{x+k} = \dfrac{k^2+k^2+k^2}{k+k} = \dfrac{3k^2}{2k} = \dfrac{3k}{2}$.

Equate the two limits:
$4 = \dfrac{3k}{2}$.

Solve for $k$:
$3k = 8 \Rightarrow k = \dfrac{8}{3}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{8}{3}$

21744.text: Given $A = \begin{bmatrix} x & 1 & -2 \end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 5 & 6 \\ 7 & 8 & 9 \end{bmatrix}$. If $ABA^t = [-20]$ then the value of $x$ is:
21744.sol:
$A = \begin{bmatrix} x & 1 & -2 \end{bmatrix}$

$B = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 5 & 6 \\ 7 & 8 & 9 \end{bmatrix}$

$AB = \begin{bmatrix} x & 1 & -2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 5 & 6 \\ 7 & 8 & 9 \end{bmatrix}$

$AB = \begin{bmatrix} x(1) + 1(4) - 2(7) & x(2) + 1(5) - 2(8) & x(3) + 1(6) - 2(9) \end{bmatrix}$

$AB = \begin{bmatrix} x - 10 & 2x - 11 & 3x - 12 \end{bmatrix}$

$ABA^t = \begin{bmatrix} x - 10 & 2x - 11 & 3x - 12 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} x \\ 1 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix}$

$ABA^t = [x(x - 10) + 1(2x - 11) - 2(3x - 12)]$

$ABA^t = [x^2 - 10x + 2x - 11 - 6x + 24]$

$ABA^t = [x^2 - 14x + 13]$

Given $ABA^t = [-20]$, we have:

$x^2 - 14x + 13 = -20$

$x^2 - 14x + 33 = 0$

$(x - 3)(x - 11) = 0$

$x = 3$ or $x = 11$

From the given options, $x = 11$.

Answer: $11$

22918.subject: Physics
22918.text: If escape velocity on earth surface is $11.1 \mathrm{ kmh}^{-1}$, then find the escape velocity on moon surface. If mass of moon is $\dfrac{1}{81}$ times of mass of earth and radius of moon is $\dfrac{1}{4}$ times radius of earth.
22918.sol:
The escape velocity $v_e$ from the surface of a planet is given by the formula $v_e = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R}}$, where $M$ is the mass of the planet and $R$ is its radius.

Let $M_e$ and $R_e$ be the mass and radius of the Earth, and $M_m$ and $R_m$ be the mass and radius of the Moon. Given $M_m = \dfrac{M_e}{81}$ and $R_m = \dfrac{R_e}{4}$.

The escape velocity on the Moon $v_m$ is given by $v_m = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM_m}{R_m}}$.

Substituting the given ratios into the expression for $v_m$:

$v_m = \sqrt{\dfrac{2G(M_e/81)}{R_e/4}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM_e}{R_e} \times \dfrac{4}{81}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM_e}{R_e}} \times \sqrt{\dfrac{4}{81}}$.

Since $v_e = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM_e}{R_e}} = 11.1 \text{ km/h}$, we have $v_m = 11.1 \times \dfrac{2}{9}$.

$v_m = 11.1 \times 0.2222... = 2.4666... \text{ km/h}$.

Rounding to two decimal places, $v_m \approx 2.47 \text{ km/h}$.

Answer: $2.47 \mathrm{ kmh}^{-1}$

23085.subject: Physics
23085.text: The percentage increase in magnetic field $\mathrm{B}$ when the space within a current carrying solenoid is filled with a medium of susceptibility 0.004 is
23085.sol:
The magnetic field inside a current-carrying solenoid in vacuum is given by $B_0 = \mu_0 n I$.

When the space is filled with a medium of magnetic susceptibility $\chi_m$, the magnetic field becomes $B = \mu_r B_0$, where $\mu_r$ is the relative permeability of the medium.

The relative permeability is related to susceptibility by $\mu_r = 1 + \chi_m$.

Given $\chi_m = 0.004$, we have $\mu_r = 1 + 0.004 = 1.004$.

The new magnetic field is $B = 1.004 B_0$.

The increase in magnetic field is $\Delta B = B - B_0 = 1.004 B_0 - B_0 = 0.004 B_0$.

The percentage increase is $\dfrac{\Delta B}{B_0} \times 100 = 0.004 \times 100 = 0.4\%$.

Answer: 0.4

23466.subject: Physics
23466.text: The zener voltage in the circuit shown is $\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{Z}}=20 \mathrm{ V}$. The load resistance $\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{L}}=5 \mathrm{k} \Omega$ and the resistance $\mathrm{R} \mathrm{s}=10 \mathrm{k} \Omega$. If the input voltage is $\mathrm{V} \mathrm{s}=100 \mathrm{ V}$, then the current through the zener diode in milliampere is:
23466.sol:
The circuit is a Zener diode voltage regulator. The Zener diode is connected in parallel with the load resistor $R_L$.

Given values:
$V_S = 100 \text{ V}$
$R_S = 10 \text{ k}\Omega = 10000 \Omega$
$R_L = 5 \text{ k}\Omega = 5000 \Omega$
$V_Z = 20 \text{ V}$

Since the Zener diode is in parallel with the load resistor $R_L$, the voltage across the load resistor $V_L$ is equal to the Zener voltage $V_Z$.
$V_L = V_Z = 20 \text{ V}$

The total current $I$ flowing through the series resistor $R_S$ is given by:
$I = \dfrac{V_S - V_Z}{R_S} = \dfrac{100 - 20}{10000} = \dfrac{80}{10000} = 8 \times 10^{-3} \text{ A} = 8 \text{ mA}$

The current flowing through the load resistor $I_L$ is:
$I_L = \dfrac{V_L}{R_L} = \dfrac{20}{5000} = 4 \times 10^{-3} \text{ A} = 4 \text{ mA}$

Applying Kirchhoff's Current Law at the node connecting $R_S$, the Zener diode, and $R_L$, the current through the Zener diode $I_Z$ is:
$I_Z = I - I_L = 8 \text{ mA} - 4 \text{ mA} = 4 \text{ mA}$

Answer: $4$

24125.subject: Mathematics
24125.text:
Let $f : \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be the function given by
$f(x) = |x - 2| + 3|x - 1| + ||x - 2| - 1|$.
What is the number of points where $f$ is NOT differentiable?
24125.sol:
The given function is $f(x) = |x - 2| + 3|x - 1| + ||x - 2| - 1|$.

The possible points of non-differentiability are the critical points where the expressions inside the absolute values become zero:
$x - 2 = 0 \Rightarrow x = 2$
$x - 1 = 0 \Rightarrow x = 1$
$|x - 2| - 1 = 0 \Rightarrow |x - 2| = 1 \Rightarrow x = 1$ or $x = 3$

Thus, the critical points to check are $x = 1, 2, 3$. Let us define $f(x)$ in the intervals around these points.

For $x < 1$:
$f(x) = (2 - x) - 3(x - 1) + (2 - x - 1)$
$f(x) = 2 - x - 3x + 3 + 1 - x = 6 - 5x$
The derivative is $f'(x) = -5$.

For $1 < x < 2$:
$f(x) = (2 - x) + 3(x - 1) - (2 - x - 1)$
$f(x) = 2 - x + 3x - 3 - 1 + x = 3x - 2$
The derivative is $f'(x) = 3$.

For $2 < x < 3$:
$f(x) = (x - 2) + 3(x - 1) - (x - 2 - 1)$
$f(x) = x - 2 + 3x - 3 - x + 3 = 3x - 2$
The derivative is $f'(x) = 3$.

For $x > 3$:
$f(x) = (x - 2) + 3(x - 1) + (x - 2 - 1)$
$f(x) = x - 2 + 3x - 3 + x - 3 = 5x - 8$
The derivative is $f'(x) = 5$.

Now, checking the differentiability at the critical points:
At $x = 1$: Left Hand Derivative (LHD) $= -5$, Right Hand Derivative (RHD) $= 3$. Since LHD \neq RHD, $ f(x)$ is not differentiable at $x = 1$.
At $x = 2$: LHD $= 3$, RHD $= 3$. Since LHD $=$ RHD, $f(x)$ is differentiable at $x = 2$.
At $x = 3$: LHD $= 3$, RHD $= 5$. Since LHD \neq RHD, $ f(x)$ is not differentiable at $x = 3$.

Therefore, there are exactly $2$ points (x = 1$ and $x = 3$) where the function is not differentiable.

Answer: 2$

27025.text:
Match the List-I with List-II
\(
List-I (Reagents)List-II (Name of reaction
involving carbonyl compounds)
A.$\mathrm{NH_2{-}NH_2, KOH}$I.Tollen's Test
B.Ag(NH_3)_2OHII.Clemmensen Reduction
C.Aq. CuSO_4,
Sodium potassium
tartarate, KOH		III.Wolff--Kishner Reduction
D.$\mathrm{Zn{-}Hg, HCl}$IV.Fehling's Test
\)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
27025.sol:
The matching of reagents with their respective named reactions is as follows:
A. $NH_2-NH_2, KOH$ (Hydrazine in basic medium) is the reagent for Wolff-Kishner Reduction, which reduces carbonyl groups to alkanes. So, A matches with III.
B. $[Ag(NH_3)_2]OH$ (Ammoniacal silver nitrate) is Tollen's reagent used for Tollen's Test to identify aldehydes. So, B matches with I.
C. Aqueous $CuSO_4$ (Fehling's A) and Sodium potassium tartarate in $KOH$ (Fehling's B) are the components of Fehling's solution used for Fehling's Test. So, C matches with IV.
D. $Zn-Hg, HCl$ (Zinc amalgam in concentrated hydrochloric acid) is the reagent for Clemmensen Reduction, which reduces carbonyl groups to alkanes. So, D matches with II.
The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

28663.text: The correct increasing order of spin-only magnetic moment values of the complex ions $\left[\mathrm{MnBr}_{4}\right]^{2-}(\mathrm{A}),\left[\mathrm{Cu}\left(\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}(\mathrm{B}),\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}\right]^{2-}(\mathrm{C})$ and $\left[\mathrm{Ni}\left(\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}(\mathrm{D})$ is :
28663.sol:
Calculate spin-only magnetic moment using $\mu_s = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$ where $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons.
For $[\text{MnBr}_4]^{2-}$ (A): Mn(II) in tetrahedral environment is high spin with 5 unpaired electrons. $\mu_s = \sqrt{5(7)} = \sqrt{35} \approx 5.92$ BM.
For $[\text{Cu}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$ (B): Cu(II) has 1 unpaired electron. $\mu_s = \sqrt{1(3)} = \sqrt{3} \approx 1.73$ BM.
For $[\text{Ni}(\text{CN})_4]^{2-}$ (C): Ni(II) in square planar geometry is low spin with 0 unpaired electrons. $\mu_s = 0$ BM.
For $[\text{Ni}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$ (D): Ni(II) in octahedral environment is high spin with 2 unpaired electrons. $\mu_s = \sqrt{2(4)} = \sqrt{8} \approx 2.83$ BM.
Increasing order: C (0) < B (1.73) < D (2.83) < A (5.92)

28788.text: The IUPAC name of ${K}_{3} [ Co ( {C}_{2}{O}_{4}{)}_{3} ]$ is:
28788.sol:
Ligands that include a numerical prefix in the name use the prefixes bis for $2$, tris for $3$, or tetrakis for $4$ to indicate their number.

If the complex ion is an anion, we drop the ending of the metal name and add –ate.

In the given coordination compound, $Co$ is the cobalt metal, ${C}_{2}{O}_{4}^{2 -}$ are the ligands named as oxalato.

The charge on $[ Co ( {C}_{2}{O}_{4}{)}_{3} ]$ is $- 3$ and oxalate is having charge of $- 2$.

$X + 3 ( - 2 ) = - 3X = + 3$

Hence, the IUPAC name of the compound ${K}_{3} [ Co ( {C}_{2}{O}_{4}{)}_{3} ]$ is Potassium trioxalatocobaltate$( III )$.

29382.subject: Chemistry
29382.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: For $KI$, molar conductivity increases steeply with dilution.

Statement II: For carbonic acid, molar conductivity increases slowly with dilution. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
29382.sol:
For strong electrolytes, ${∧}_{m}$ increases slowly with dilution and can be represented by the equation:

${∧}_{m} = {∧}_{m}^{o} - Ac\dfrac{1}{2}$

It can be seen that if we plot ${∧}_{m}$ against $c\dfrac{1}{2}$, We obtain a straight line with intercept equal to ${∧}_{m}$ and slope equal to '$- A$'. The value of the constant '$A$' for a given solvent and temperature depends on the type of electrolyte. $KI$ is a strong electrolyte.

Weak electrolytes like carbonic acid and have lower degree of dissociation at higher concentrations and hence for such electrolytes, the change in ${∧}_{m}$ with dilution is due to increase in the degree of dissociation and consequently the number of ions in total volume of solution that contains $1mol$ of electrolyte. In such cases ${∧}_{m}$ increases steeply on dilution, especially near lower concentrations. Therefore, ${∧}_{m}^{o}$ cannot be obtained by extrapolation of ${∧}_{m}$ to zero concentration.

According to Bohr's angular momentum equation,

$mvr = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi}$

The angular momentum equation for third orbit is

$mvr = \dfrac{3h}{2\pi}$

$\dfrac{2\pir}{3} = \dfrac{h}{mv}$

According de Broglie's equation

$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{mv}$

$∴ \lambda = \dfrac{2\pi9{a}_{0}}{3} = 6\pi{a}_{0}$

32429.subject: Chemistry
32429.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion $A$ and the other is labelled as Reason $R$

Assertion $A$ : Dissolved substances can be removed from a colloidal solution by diffusion through a parchment paper.

Reason $R$ : Particles in a true solution cannot pass through parchment paper but the collodial particles can pass through the parchment paper.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both $A$ and $R$ are correct and $R$ is the correct explanation of $A$
Both $A$ and $R$ are correct but $R$ is not the correct explanation of $A$
$A$ is correct but $R$ is not correct
$A$ is not correct but $R$ is correct
32429.sol:
Colloidal solution particles can be separated using parchment paper. Since Particles (ions or smaller molecules) in a true solution can pass through animal membrane (bladder) or parchment paper or cellophane sheet but not the colloidal particles, the membrane can be used for dialysis.A bag of suitable membrane containing the colloidal solution is suspended in a vessel through which fresh water is continuously flowing (Fig. 5.9). The molecules and ions diffuse through membrane into the outer water and pure colloidal solution is left behind.

Hence, assertion is correct but reason is incorrect

33455.text: The natural number $m$, for which the coefficient of $x$ in the binomial expansion of  ${\left({x}^{m} + \dfrac{1}{{x}^{2}}\right)}^{22}$ is 1540, is
33455.sol:
The general term in the binomial expansion,

${T}_{r + 1} = Cr 22 {\left({x}^{m}\right)}^{22 - r}{x}^{- 2r}$

$⇒ {T}_{r + 1} = Cr 22 {x}^{m ( 22 - r ) - 2r}$

For the coefficient of $x$

$22m - mr - 2r = 1$

$⇒ 22m - 1 = r ( m + 2 )$

$⇒ r = \dfrac{22m - 1}{m + 2}$

$⇒ r = \dfrac{22m + 44 - 45}{m + 2}$

$r = 22 - \dfrac{3 . 3 . 5}{m + 2} ⇒ 22 - r = \dfrac{3 \cdot 3 \cdot 5}{m + 2}$

Since, $Cr 22 = C22 - r 22$

So possible values of $m = 1, 3, 7, 13, 43$, but $C3 22 = 1540 ⇒ 22 - r = 3 ⇒ m = 13$

33996.text: Consider the function $f: \left(0, \infty\right) \to R$ defined by $f\left(x\right) = {e}^{- \left|{\log}_{e}x\right|}$. If $m$ and $n$ be respectively the number of points at which $f$ is not continuous and $f$ is not differentiable, then $m + n$ is
33996.sol:
We know that, $\left|logx\right|$ is continuous in $\left(0, \infty\right)$.

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = {e}^{- log\left|x\right|}$ is continuous in $\left(0, \infty\right)$

Thus, the number of points where $f\left(x\right)$ is discontinuous is $0$.

$⇒ m = 0$

$f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}{e}^{logx}, & 0 < x < 1 \\ {e}^{- logx}, & x \ge 1\end{cases}\right)

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}x, & 0 < x < 1 \\ \dfrac{1}{x}, & x \ge 1\end{cases}\right)

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}1, & 0 < x < 1 \\ \dfrac{- 1}{{x}^{2}}, & x \ge 1\end{cases}\right)

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left({1}^{-}\right) = 1 \text{ and } {f}^{'}\left({1}^{+}\right) = - 1$

So, the number of points where $f\left(x\right)$ is non-differentiable is $1$.

$⇒ n = 1$

$⇒ m + n = 1$

34286.text: If $\left[x\right]$ is the greatest integer $\le x,$ then ${\pi}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{2}\left(sin\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right){\left(x - \left[x\right]\right)}^{[ x ]}dx$ is equal to :
34286.sol:
Let, $I = {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{2}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right){\left(x - \left[x\right]\right)}^{[ x ]}dx$

$I = {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right){\left(x - \left[x\right]\right)}^{[ x ]}dx + {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{1}^{2}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right){\left(x - \left[x\right]\right)}^{[ x ]}dx$

$I = {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right){x}^{0}dx + {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{1}^{2}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right){\left(x - 1\right)}^{1}dx$

$I = {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)dx + {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{1}^{2}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)\left(x - 1\right)dx$

$I = {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)dx + {\pi}^{2}\left[x{∫}_{1}^{2}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right) d x - {∫}_{1}^{2}\left\{\dfrac{d}{dx}x{∫}_{1}^{2}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)dx\right\}dx\right] - {\pi}^{2}{∫}_{1}^{2}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)dx$

$I = {\pi}^{2}{\left[- \dfrac{2}{\pi}cos\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)\right]}_{0}^{1} + {\pi}^{2}{\left[\left(x\right)\dfrac{2}{\pi}\right \left(- cos\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)\right)}_{1}^{2}\left- {∫}_{1}^{2}\dfrac{2}{\pi}\left(- cos\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)dx\right] + {\pi}^{2} \times \dfrac{2}{\pi}{\left[cos\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{2}\right)\right]}_{1}^{2}$

$I = {\pi}^{2}{\left[- \dfrac{2}{\pi}cos\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)\right]}_{0}^{1} + {\pi}^{2}{\left[\left(x\right)\dfrac{2}{\pi}\right \left(- cos\left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)\right)}_{1}^{2}\left+ {\left(\dfrac{2}{\pi}\right)}^{2}{\left[sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{2}\right)\right]}_{1}^{2}\right] + {\pi}^{2} \times \dfrac{2}{\pi}{\left[cos\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{2}\right)\right]}_{1}^{2}$

$I = - {\pi}^{2}\left[\dfrac{2}{\pi}cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) - \dfrac{2}{\pi}cos\left(0\right)\right] + {\pi}^{2}\left[2 \times \dfrac{2}{\pi}\left(- cos\pi\right) + 1 \times \dfrac{2}{\pi} \times \left(cos\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\right]\left+ 4\left[sin\left(\pi\right) - sin\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]\right] + {\pi}^{2} \times \dfrac{2}{\pi}\left[cos\left(\pi\right) - cos\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$

$I = 2\pi + 4\pi + 4 ( 0 - 1 ) - 2\pi$

$I = 4\pi - 4$

$I = 4\left(\pi - 1\right)$

34594.text:
If the system of linear equations

$x + ky + 3z = 0$
$3x + ky - 2z = 0$
$2x + 4y - 3z = 0$

has a non-zero solution $\left(x, y, z\right),$ then $\dfrac{xz}{{y}^{2}}$ is equal to:
34594.sol:
$\left|\begin{cases}1 & k & 3 \\ 3 & k & - 2 \\ 2 & 4 & - 3\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left(- 3k + 8\right) - 3\left(- 3k - 12\right) + 2\left(- 5k\right) = 0$

$⇒ - 4k + 44 = 0$ $⇒$ $k = 11$

$⇒ x + 11y + 3z = 0 . . . \left(1\right)$

$⇒ 3x + 11y - 2z = 0 . . . \left(2\right)$

$⇒ 2x + 4y - 3z = 0 . . . \left(3\right)$

On solving equations$\left(1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$, we get

$2x - 5z = 0$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{5z}{2}$

Put it in equation $\left(3\right)$, we get

$2z + 4y = 0$

$⇒ z = - 2y$

$∴ \dfrac{xz}{{y}^{2}} = \dfrac{\left(- 2y\right) \times \left(- 5y\right)}{{y}^{2}} = 10$

35397.text: Let the foci and length of the latus rectum of an ellipse $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} = 1$, $a > b$ be $\left(\pm 5, 0\right)$ and $\sqrt{50}$, respectively. Then, the square of the eccentricity of the hyperbola $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} - \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{a}^{2}{b}^{2}} = 1$ equals
35397.sol:
Given,

Ellipse $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} = 1$

And its focii $≡ \left(\pm 5, 0\right)$ and its latusrectum $\dfrac{2{b}^{2}}{a} = \sqrt{50}$

So, $ae = 5$ and ${b}^{2} = \dfrac{5\sqrt{2}a}{2}$

Now, using the formula eccentricity we get,

${b}^{2} = {a}^{2}\left(1 - {e}^{2}\right) = \dfrac{5\sqrt{2}a}{2}$

$⇒ a\left(1 - {e}^{2}\right) = \dfrac{5\sqrt{2}}{2}$ $\left\{\text{as}a \ne 0\right\}$

$⇒ \dfrac{5}{e}\left(1 - {e}^{2}\right) = \dfrac{5\sqrt{2}}{2}$

$⇒ \sqrt{2} - \sqrt{2}{e}^{2} = e$

$⇒ \sqrt{2}{e}^{2} + e - \sqrt{2} = 0$

$⇒ \sqrt{2}{e}^{2} + 2e - e - \sqrt{2} = 0$

$⇒ \sqrt{2}e\left(e + \sqrt{2}\right) - 1\left(1 + \sqrt{2}\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(e + \sqrt{2}\right)\left(\sqrt{2}e - 1\right) = 0$

$∴ e \ne - \sqrt{2}; e = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$⇒ a = 5\sqrt{2}$ and $b = 5$

Now, finding eccentricity of hyperbola,

$\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} - \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{a}^{2}{b}^{2}} = 1$ 

We know that formula of eccentricity of hyperbola is given by, ${B}^{2} = {A}^{2}\left({{e}_{H}}^{2} - 1\right)$ where ${A}^{2} = {b}^{2} \text{ and } {B}^{2} = {a}^{2}{b}^{2}$

$⇒ {a}^{2}{b}^{2} = {b}^{2}\left({e}_{H}^{2} - 1\right)$

$⇒ {a}^{2} = \left({e}_{H}^{2} - 1\right)$

$⇒ 50 = \left({e}_{H}^{2} - 1\right)$

$⇒ {e}_{H}^{2} = 51$

36179.subject: Mathematics
36179.text: Let $A,B$ and $C$ be the vertices of a variable right angled triangle inscribed in the parabola $y^2=16x$. Let the vertex $B$ containing the right angle be $(4,8)$ and the locus of the centroid of $\triangle ABC$ be a conic $C_o$. Then three times the length of latus rectum of $C_o$ is ______
36179.sol:
The equation of the parabola is $y^2 = 16x$, which gives $a = 4$. Any point on the parabola can be taken as $(4t^2, 8t)$.

The vertex $B$ is given as $(4,8)$, which corresponds to the parameter $t = 1$. Let the parameters for vertices $A$ and $C$ be $t_1$ and $t_2$ respectively. Thus, $A \equiv (4t_1^2, 8t_1)$ and $C \equiv (4t_2^2, 8t_2)$.

The slope of $AB$ is:
$m_{AB} = \dfrac{8t_1 - 8}{4t_1^2 - 4} = \dfrac{2(t_1 - 1)}{(t_1 - 1)(t_1 + 1)} = \dfrac{2}{t_1 + 1}$

Similarly, the slope of $BC$ is:
$m_{BC} = \dfrac{2}{t_2 + 1}$

Since $\triangle ABC$ is right-angled at $B$, $AB \perp BC$. Therefore, $m_{AB} \times m_{BC} = -1$:
$\dfrac{2}{t_1 + 1} \times \dfrac{2}{t_2 + 1} = -1$
$(t_1 + 1)(t_2 + 1) = -4$
$t_1t_2 + t_1 + t_2 + 5 = 0$

Let the centroid of $\triangle ABC$ be $(h, k)$. Then:
$h = \dfrac{4 + 4t_1^2 + 4t_2^2}{3} \Rightarrow t_1^2 + t_2^2 = \dfrac{3h}{4} - 1$
$k = \dfrac{8 + 8t_1 + 8t_2}{3} \Rightarrow t_1 + t_2 = \dfrac{3k}{8} - 1$

From the perpendicularity condition, we can express $t_1t_2$ as:
$t_1t_2 = -5 - (t_1 + t_2) = -5 - \left(\dfrac{3k}{8} - 1\right) = -4 - \dfrac{3k}{8}$

Using the algebraic identity $t_1^2 + t_2^2 = (t_1 + t_2)^2 - 2t_1t_2$, we substitute the expressions in terms of $k$:
$\dfrac{3h}{4} - 1 = \left(\dfrac{3k}{8} - 1\right)^2 - 2\left(-4 - \dfrac{3k}{8}\right)$
$\dfrac{3h}{4} - 1 = \dfrac{9k^2}{64} - \dfrac{3k}{4} + 1 + 8 + \dfrac{3k}{4}$
$\dfrac{3h}{4} - 1 = \dfrac{9k^2}{64} + 9$
$\dfrac{3h}{4} = \dfrac{9k^2}{64} + 10$
$3h = \dfrac{9k^2}{16} + 40$
$\dfrac{9k^2}{16} = 3h - 40$
$k^2 = \dfrac{16}{9}(3h - 40) = \dfrac{16}{3}\left(h - \dfrac{40}{3}\right)$

Replacing $(h, k)$ with $(x, y)$, the locus $C_o$ is the parabola:
$y^2 = \dfrac{16}{3}\left(x - \dfrac{40}{3}\right)$

The length of the latus rectum of this parabola is $\dfrac{16}{3}$.

Three times the length of the latus rectum is $3 \times \dfrac{16}{3} = 16$.

Answer: $16$

38812.text:
A coil of inductance $1H$ and resistance $100Ω$ is connected to a battery of $6V$. Determine approximately :

(a) The time elapsed before the current acquires half of its steady-state value
(b) The energy stored in the magnetic field associated with the coil at an instant $15ms$ after the circuit is switched on. (Given $ln2 = 0 . 693$, $e\dfrac{- 3}{2} = 0 . 25$)
38812.sol:
Given circuit is $R - L$ growth circuit

The current is the circuit is given by,

$i = \dfrac{E}{R}\left(1 - {e}^{- \dfrac{t}{τ}}\right)$

For current to be half of the peak value,

$i = \dfrac{E}{2R} = \dfrac{E}{R}\left(1 - {e}^{- \dfrac{t}{τ}}\right)$

Solving $t = τln2$

$t = \dfrac{L}{R}ln2 = \dfrac{1}{100}0 . 693 = 0 . 00693$$≃ 7ms$

At time $t = 15ms$,

$i\left(15ms\right) = \dfrac{E}{R}\left(1 - {e}^{- \dfrac{15}{10}}\right)$

$⇒ i = \dfrac{6}{100}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{4}\right) = \dfrac{3}{4} \times \dfrac{6}{100} = 0 . 045A$

$⇒ U = \dfrac{1}{2}L{i}^{2}$

by solving we get $U = 1mJ$.

Which of the following are true?

A. Speed of light in vacuum is dependent on the direction of propagation.

B. Speed of light in a medium is independent of the wavelength of light.

Speed of light in vaccum is independent of the frequency, wavelength, nature of the source, direction of propagation, motion of the source and intensity of the wave. But it depends on the refractive index of the medium.

Therefore, the speed of light in vacuum is a universal constant.

Hence, C and D are only correct.

44255.text: The width of fringe is $2mm$ on the screen in a double slit experiment for the light of wavelength of $400nm$. The width of the fringe for the light of wavelength $600nm$ will be:
44255.sol:
For a light of wavelength $\lambda$, the fringe width in double slit experiment is given by

$\beta = \dfrac{\lambdaD}{d} . . . ( 1 )$

For a light of wavelength $\lambda '$, the fringe width is given by

$\beta ' = \dfrac{\lambda ' D}{d} . . . \left(2\right)$

Divide equation (2) by equation (1) and simplify to obtain the fringe width for the later case.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{\beta '}{\beta} & = & \dfrac{\dfrac{\lambda ' D}{d}}{\dfrac{\lambdaD}{d}} \\ & = & \dfrac{\lambda '}{\lambda} \\ & ⇒ & \beta ' = \dfrac{\lambda '}{\lambda}\beta . . . \left(3\right)\end{cases}$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (3) to calculate the required fringe width.

$\begin{cases}\beta ' & = & \dfrac{600nm}{400nm} \times 2mm \\ & = & 3mm\end{cases}$

44557.subject: Physics
44557.text: A smooth inclined plane ends in a vertical circular loop, as shown in the figure. A small body is released from height $h$ as shown. If the body exerts a force of three times its weight on the plane at the highest point of circle then the height $h = \alpha R$. The value of $\alpha$ is _______.
44557.sol:
Let $v$ be the velocity of the body at the highest point of the circular loop.

At the highest point, the forces acting on the body are its weight $mg$ (downwards) and the normal reaction $N$ (downwards). The net downward force provides the necessary centripetal acceleration:

$N + mg = \dfrac{mv^2}{R}$

Given that the body exerts a force equal to three times its weight on the track at the highest point, we have $N = 3mg$. Substituting this into the equation:

$3mg + mg = \dfrac{mv^2}{R}$

$4mg = \dfrac{mv^2}{R} \Rightarrow v^2 = 4gR$

Applying the principle of conservation of mechanical energy between the point of release and the highest point of the loop (which is at a height of $2R$ from the bottom):

$mgh = mg(2R) + \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2$

Substituting $v^2 = 4gR$ into the energy equation:

$mgh = 2mgR + \dfrac{1}{2}m(4gR)$

$mgh = 2mgR + 2mgR = 4mgR$

Therefore, $h = 4R$.

Comparing this with the given relation $h = \alpha R$, we get $\alpha = 4$.

Answer: $4$

The kinetic energy of a moving particle is given by

$\begin{cases}nE & = & \dfrac{1}{2}m\left\{( 2u{)}^{2} - {u}^{2}\right\} \\ & = & \dfrac{1}{2}m\left(3{u}^{2}\right) . . . \left(2\right)\end{cases}$

Divide equation (2) by equation (1) and solve to calculate the value of $n$.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{nE}{E} & = & \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}m\left(3{u}^{2}\right)}{\dfrac{1}{2}m{u}^{2}} \\ & ⇒ & n = 3\end{cases}$

45893.subject: Chemistry
45893.text: Which of the following would exert maximum osmotic pressure?
options: A solution obtained by mixing equal volumes of (2) and (3) and filtering
45893.sol:
Osmotic pressure is a colligative property, i.e., depends upon the number of particles of solute. Thus, the solution in which solute gives maximum number of ions, exerts maximum osmotic pressure. Number of particles,
(1) In decinormal aluminium sulphate
$\mathrm{Al}_2\left(\mathrm{SO}_4\right)_3 \longrightarrow \underbrace{2 \mathrm{Al}^{3+}+3 \mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}}_{5 \text{ particles }}$
(2) In decinormal barium chloride,
$\mathrm{BaCl}_2 \longrightarrow \underbrace{\mathrm{Ba}^{2+}+2 \mathrm{Cl}^{-}}_{3 \text{ particles }}$
(3) In decinormal sodium chloride,
$\mathrm{NaCl} \longrightarrow \underbrace{\mathrm{Na}^{+}+\mathrm{Cl}^{-}}_{2 \text{ particles }}$
(4) When equal volumes of (2) and (3) are mixed, the concentration becomes half of present concentration.
Thus, decinormal aluminium sulphate exerts maximum osmotic pressure.

54576.subject: Physics
54576.text: Two pendulums of time periods 3 s and 7 s , respectively start oscillating simultaneously from two opposite extreme positions. After how much time they will be in same phase?
54576.sol:
General equation of oscillation are
$\begin{aligned}
& y_1=A \sin \left(\omega_1 t+\frac{\pi}{2}\right) \\
& y_2=A \sin \left(\omega_2 t+\frac{\pi}{2}\right)
\end{aligned}$
Now, $\omega_1 t+\frac{\pi}{2}=\omega_2 t-\frac{\pi}{2}$ or $\begin{aligned}
t & =\frac{\pi}{\omega_2-\omega_1} \\
& =\frac{\pi}{\left(2 \pi / T_2\right)-\left(2 \pi / T_1\right)} \\
& =\frac{T_1 T_2}{2\left(T_1-T_2\right)} \\
& =\frac{3 \times 7}{2(7-3)}=\frac{21}{8} \mathrm{ s}
\end{aligned}$

55293.subject: Chemistry
55293.text: Which from following compounds is an example of secondary amine?
55293.sol:
Identifying the secondary amine requires examining nitrogen atom bonding patterns. Secondary amines feature two alkyl or aryl groups attached to the nitrogen atom.

Ethane-1,2-diamine ($\text{H}_2\text{N}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{NH}_2$) contains primary amine groups, as each nitrogen bonds to one alkyl group and two hydrogens.

Propan-2-amine ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{NH}_2)-\text{CH}_3$) is also primary, with nitrogen bonded to one isopropyl group and two hydrogens.

N-Methylmethanamine ($\text{CH}_3-\text{NH}-\text{CH}_3$) matches the secondary amine definition: nitrogen bonded to two methyl groups and one hydrogen.

N,N-Dimethylmethanamine ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{N}$) is tertiary, with nitrogen bonded to three methyl groups.

$\boxed{\text{C}}$ is the secondary amine.

55756.text: Which among the following molecule exhibits paramagnetism?
55756.sol:
According to Molecular Orbital Theory, the electronic configuration of $\text{O}_2$ (16 electrons) is:

${\sigma_{1s}}^2 {{\sigma^{*}}_{1s}}^2 \sigma_{2s}^2 {{\sigma^{*}}_{2s}}^2 {\sigma_{2p_z}}^2 {\pi_{2p_x}}^2 {\pi_{2p_y}}^2 {{\pi^{*}}_{2p_x}}^1 {{\pi^{*}}_{2p_y}}^1$

Due to the presence of two unpaired electrons in the degenerate antibonding $\pi^{*}$ molecular orbitals, $\text{O}_2$ is paramagnetic.

$\text{N}_2$ (14 electrons) and $\text{F}_2$ (18 electrons) have all their electrons paired in their molecular orbitals, making them diamagnetic.

55761.subject: Chemistry
55761.text: Which of the following compound has square pyramidal structure?
55761.sol:
The shape of the molecules can be determined using VSEPR theory by calculating the number of bond pairs (bp) and lone pairs (lp) on the central Xenon (Xe) atom, which has 8 valence electrons.

For $\text{XeF}_4$: Xe forms 4 single bonds with F atoms, using 4 electrons. Remaining electrons = 4 (2 lone pairs). With 4 bp and 2 lp, the hybridization is $sp^3d^2$ and the shape is square planar.

For $\text{XeF}_6$: Xe forms 6 single bonds with F atoms, using 6 electrons. Remaining electrons = 2 (1 lone pair). With 6 bp and 1 lp, the hybridization is $sp^3d^3$ and the shape is distorted octahedral.

For $\text{XeO}_3$: Xe forms 3 double bonds with O atoms, using 6 electrons. Remaining electrons = 2 (1 lone pair). With 3 bp ($\sigma$-bonds) and 1 lp, the hybridization is $sp^3$ and the shape is trigonal pyramidal.

For $\text{XeOF}_4$: Xe forms 1 double bond with O and 4 single bonds with F, using $2 + 4 = 6$ electrons. Remaining electrons = 2 (1 lone pair). With 5 bp ($\sigma$-bonds) and 1 lp, the hybridization is $sp^3d^2$ and the shape is square pyramidal.

Answer: $\text{XeOF}_4$

56409.text: Which from following complexes is an example of $\text{MA}_4\text{BC}$ type distereoisomers ?
56409.sol:
The general formula $\text{MA}_4\text{BC}$ represents an octahedral complex with one central metal atom $\text{M}$, four identical ligands $\text{A}$, and two different ligands $\text{B}$ and $\text{C}$.

Analyzing the given options:

$[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)(\text{H}_2\text{O})\,\text{Cl}_2]$ is of the type $\text{MA}_2\text{BC}$ (where $\text{A} = \text{Cl}$, $\text{B} = \text{NH}_3$, $\text{C} = \text{H}_2\text{O}$).

$[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_4\,\text{ClBr}]^{2+}$ is of the type $\text{MA}_4\text{BC}$ (where $\text{A} = \text{NH}_3$, $\text{B} = \text{Cl}$, $\text{C} = \text{Br}$).

$\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2\,\text{Cl}_2$ is of the type $\text{MA}_2\text{B}_2$ (where $\text{A} = \text{NH}_3$, $\text{B} = \text{Cl}$).

$[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_4\,\text{Cl}_2]^+$ is of the type $\text{MA}_4\text{B}_2$ (where $\text{A} = \text{NH}_3$, $\text{B} = \text{Cl}$).

Thus, $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_4\,\text{ClBr}]^{2+}$ is the example of $\text{MA}_4\text{BC}$ type complex, which exhibits geometrical isomerism (cis and trans forms), and these geometrical isomers are diastereoisomers.

56863.subject: Chemistry
56863.text:
Consider galvanic cell,
${ }^{\ominus} \mathrm{A}_{(\mathrm{s})}\left|\mathrm{A}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{+2}\right|\left|\mathrm{B}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{+}\right| \mathrm{B}_{(\mathrm{s})}^{\oplus}$
if emf of cell is positive, identify a correct cell reaction from following.
56863.sol:
Cell notation follows the convention: anode | anode ions || cathode ions | cathode. The anode is written on the left (marked as negative) where oxidation occurs, and the cathode on the right (marked as positive) where reduction occurs.

Given the notation $\mathrm{A}_{(\mathrm{s})}^{\ominus} | \mathrm{A}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{+2} || \mathrm{B}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{+} | \mathrm{B}_{(\mathrm{s})}^{\oplus}$, the half-reactions are:

Oxidation: $\mathrm{A}_{(\mathrm{s})} \rightarrow \mathrm{A}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{+2} + 2\mathrme^{-}$

Reduction: $\mathrm{B}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{+} + \mathrme^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{B}_{(\mathrm{s})}$

To balance electrons, multiply the reduction half-reaction by 2:

$2\mathrm{B}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{+} + 2\mathrme^{-} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{B}_{(\mathrm{s})}$

Combining gives the cell reaction:

$\mathrm{A}_{(\mathrm{s})} + 2\mathrm{B}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{+} \rightarrow \mathrm{A}_{(\mathrm{aq})}^{+2} + 2\mathrm{B}_{(\mathrm{s})}$

This matches Option B.

58031.subject: Chemistry
58031.text: The solubility product of $\mathrm{PbI}_2$ is $1.08 \times 10^{-7}$. Calculate its solubility in $\mathrm{mol } \mathrm{dm}^{-3}$ at 298 K ?
58031.sol:
The dissociation equilibrium for $\mathrm{PbI}_2$ is established as:

$\mathrm{PbI}_2(s) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{Pb}^{2+}(aq) + 2\mathrm{I}^{-}(aq)$

Define $s$ as the molar solubility in $\mathrm{mol dm}^{-3}$, which yields $[\mathrm{Pb}^{2+}] = s$ and $[\mathrm{I}^{-}] = 2s$.

The solubility product is $K_{sp} = [\mathrm{Pb}^{2+}][\mathrm{I}^{-}]^2 = s \cdot (2s)^2 = 4s^3$.

Given $K_{sp} = 1.08 \times 10^{-7}$, solve for $s$:

$4s^3 = 1.08 \times 10^{-7}$

$s^3 = 2.7 \times 10^{-8}$

$s = \sqrt[3]{2.7 \times 10^{-8}} \approx 3 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{mol dm}^{-3}$

The calculated solubility corresponds to option D.

59761.subject: Chemistry
59761.text: Which of the following is a water-in-oil type of emulsion?
59761.sol:
Emulsions are colloidal systems in which both the dispersed phase and the dispersion medium are liquids.

In a water-in-oil (W/O) emulsion, water is the dispersed phase and oil is the dispersion medium.

Butter is an example of a water-in-oil emulsion, where water is dispersed in fat (oil).

Milk and vanishing cream are examples of oil-in-water (O/W) emulsions, where oil is dispersed in water.

Answer: Butter

60283.subject: Mathematics
60283.text: If the curves $y^2=6 x$ and $9 x^2+$ by ^2=16 intersect each other at right angles, then the value of b is
60283.sol:
The curves $C_1: y^2 = 6x$ and $C_2: 9x^2 + by^2 = 16$ intersect orthogonally when the product of their tangent slopes at the intersection point $(x_0, y_0)$ equals $-1$.

For $C_1$, $2y \frac{dy}{dx} = 6$ so the slope is $\frac{dy}{dx}_1 = \frac{3}{y_0}$.
For $C_2$, $18x + 2by \frac{dy}{dx} = 0$ so the slope is $\frac{dy}{dx}_2 = \frac{-9x_0}{by_0}$.

The orthogonality condition gives $(\frac{3}{y_0})(\frac{-9x_0}{by_0}) = -1$, which simplifies to $27x_0 = by_0^2$.

Since $(x_0, y_0)$ lies on $C_1$, we have $y_0^2 = 6x_0$. Substituting yields $27x_0 = b(6x_0)$.

If $x_0 = 0$, then $C_2$ gives $0 = 16$, a contradiction. Thus $x_0 \neq 0$ and we can divide both sides by $x_0$, obtaining $27 = 6b$ and consequently $b = \frac{9}{2}$.

The value is $\boxed{D}$.

61039.subject: Mathematics
61039.text: If $\int_0^a (x^2 - 4x + 1)dx = 6$, then the real value of $a$ is
61039.sol:
Evaluating the given definite integral:

$\int_0^a (x^2 - 4x + 1)dx = \left[ \dfrac{x^3}{3} - 2x^2 + x \right]_0^a$

Substituting the limits, we get:

$\dfrac{a^3}{3} - 2a^2 + a = 6$

Multiplying by $3$ on both sides:

$a^3 - 6a^2 + 3a - 18 = 0$

Factorizing the polynomial:

$a^2(a - 6) + 3(a - 6) = 0$

$(a^2 + 3)(a - 6) = 0$

Since $a$ is a real number, $a^2 + 3 \neq 0$.

Therefore, $a - 6 = 0 \Rightarrow a = 6$.

Answer: $6$

61044.text: If $\int_1^a (2x + 1) dx = 5$, then the sum of the values of $a$ is..

Evaluating the definite integral:

$\int_1^a (2x + 1) dx = [x^2 + x]_1^a$

Substituting the limits:

$(a^2 + a) - (1^2 + 1) = 5$

$a^2 + a - 2 = 5$

$a^2 + a - 7 = 0$

This is a quadratic equation in $a$. The sum of the roots of the equation is $-\dfrac{1}{1} = -1$.

Answer: $-1$

61300.subject: Mathematics
61300.text: The solution of the differential equation $x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = x^3 y^6$, is...
61300.sol:
The given differential equation is:

$x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = x^3 y^6$

Dividing the entire equation by $x y^6$:

$\dfrac{1}{y^6} \dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{1}{x y^5} = x^2$

Let $v = \dfrac{1}{y^5} = y^{-5}$.

Differentiating with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{dv}{dx} = -5 y^{-6} \dfrac{dy}{dx} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{y^6} \dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{1}{5} \dfrac{dv}{dx}$

Substituting this into the differential equation:

$-\dfrac{1}{5} \dfrac{dv}{dx} + \dfrac{1}{x} v = x^2$

$\dfrac{dv}{dx} - \dfrac{5}{x} v = -5 x^2$

This is a linear differential equation of the form $\dfrac{dv}{dx} + P v = Q$, where $P = -\dfrac{5}{x}$ and $Q = -5 x^2$.

The Integrating Factor (IF) is:

$IF = e^{\int -\dfrac{5}{x} dx} = e^{-5 \ln x} = x^{-5}$

The solution is given by:

$v \cdot x^{-5} = \int (-5 x^2) \cdot x^{-5} dx + c$

$v x^{-5} = \int -5 x^{-3} dx + c$

$v x^{-5} = -5 \left( \dfrac{x^{-2}}{-2} \right) + c$

$v x^{-5} = \dfrac{5}{2} x^{-2} + c$

Multiplying both sides by $x^5$:

$v = \dfrac{5}{2} x^3 + c x^5$

Substituting back $v = \dfrac{1}{y^5}$:

$\dfrac{1}{y^5} = \dfrac{5}{2} x^3 + c x^5$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{y^5} = \dfrac{5}{2}x^3 + cx^5$

63492.subject: Mathematics
63492.text: There are $5$ boys and $3$ girls seated in a row for a photograph. The number of ways in which a photograph can be taken if the girls occupy only odd places is...
63492.sol:
Total number of persons is $5 + 3 = 8$.

The seats are numbered $1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8$.

The odd places are $1, 3, 5, 7$. There are $4$ odd places.

The $3$ girls can be seated in these $4$ odd places in ^{4}P_{3}$ ways.

^{4}P_{3} = 24$

After seating the girls, there are $5$ seats remaining (1$ odd and 4$ even places).

The $5$ boys can be seated in the remaining $5$ places in $5!$ ways.

$5! = 120$

Total number of ways $= 24 \times 120 = 2880$.

Answer: $2880$

63563.subject: Mathematics
63563.text: In an entrance test, there are multiple choice questions. There are four possible answers to each question, only one of which is correct. The probability that a student knows the answer to a question is 90%. If he gets the correct answer to a question, then the probability that he was guessing is
63563.sol:
Let $E_1$ be the event that the student knows the answer and $E_2$ be the event that the student guesses the answer.

$P(E_1) = \dfrac{90}{100} = \dfrac{9}{10}$

$P(E_2) = 1 - P(E_1) = \dfrac{1}{10}$

Let $A$ be the event that the student gets the correct answer.

If the student knows the answer, the probability of getting it correct is $1$, so $P(A|E_1) = 1$.

If the student guesses, since there are $4$ options and only $1$ is correct, the probability of getting it correct is $\dfrac{1}{4}$, so $P(A|E_2) = \dfrac{1}{4}$.

By Bayes' theorem, the probability that the student was guessing given that he got the correct answer is:

$P(E_2|A) = \dfrac{P(E_2)P(A|E_2)}{P(E_1)P(A|E_1) + P(E_2)P(A|E_2)}$

$P(E_2|A) = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{10} \times \dfrac{1}{4}}{\dfrac{9}{10} \times 1 + \dfrac{1}{10} \times \dfrac{1}{4}}$

$P(E_2|A) = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{40}}{\dfrac{36}{40} + \dfrac{1}{40}} = \dfrac{1}{37}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{37}$

63607.text: The probability that an event A happens in a trial is 0.4. If three independent trials are made, then the probability that A happens at least once is
63607.sol:
Given the probability of event $A$ as $P(A) = 0.4$, the complement is $P(A') = 1 - P(A) = 0.6$.

For three independent trials, the probability that $A$ occurs at least once is found using the complement rule: $1 - P(A' \text{ in all three trials}) = 1 - (0.6)^3 = 0.784$.

The provided options—7.856, 7.452, 7.545, 7.752—are invalid as probabilities but, when scaled by $\frac{1}{10}$, become 0.7856, 0.7452, 0.7545, 0.7752. The calculated result $0.784$ is closest to 0.7856.

65192.text: If the points $\mathrm{A}(1,1,2), \mathrm{B}(2,1, \mathrm{p}), \mathrm{C}(1,0,3)$ and $\mathrm{D}(2,2,0)$ are coplanar then the value of $p$ is
65192.sol:
Four points are coplanar if the scalar triple product of vectors from one point to the other three is zero.

From point A(1,1,2), the vectors are:

$\vec{AB} = (1, 0, p-2)$

$\vec{AC} = (0, -1, 1)$

$\vec{AD} = (1, 1, -2)$

The scalar triple product $[\vec{AB} \vec{AC} \vec{AD}]$ equals the determinant:

\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 0 & p-2 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -2 \end{vmatrix} = 0$

Evaluating the determinant yields:

1 \cdot (2 - 1) + (p-2) \cdot (0 + 1) = 0$

$1 + p - 2 = 0$

$p = 1$

The points are coplanar when $p = 1$, corresponding to option C.

65869.text: If 'E' and 'L' denote the magnitude of total energy and angular momentum of revolving electron in $n^{th}$ Bohr orbit then
65869.sol:
The magnitude of total energy of an electron in the $n^{th}$ Bohr orbit is given by $E \propto \dfrac{1}{n^2}$.

The angular momentum of the electron in the $n^{th}$ Bohr orbit is given by $L = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi}$.

This implies $L \propto n$.

Substituting $n \propto L$ in the expression for energy, we get $E \propto \dfrac{1}{L^2}$.

Thus, $E \propto L^{-2}$.

Answer: $E \propto L^{-2}$

66571.text: Electron beam when accelerated by a voltage of 10 kV , has a de-Broglie wavelength ' $\lambda$ '. If the voltage is increased to 20 kV then the de-Broglie wavelength associated with the electron beam would be
66571.sol:
The de-Broglie wavelength $\lambda$ for a particle with momentum $p$ is given by $\lambda = h/p$, where $h$ is Planck's constant.

For an electron accelerated through potential difference $V$, the kinetic energy $eV$ equals $p^2/(2m)$, yielding $p = \sqrt{2meV}$. Substituting into the wavelength formula gives $\lambda = h/\sqrt{2meV}$.

The wavelength scales as $\lambda \propto 1/\sqrt{V}$. For voltages $V_1 = 10 \text{ kV}$ and $V_2 = 20 \text{ kV}$, the ratio is:

$\frac{\lambda_2}{\lambda_1} = \sqrt{\frac{V_1}{V_2}} = \sqrt{\frac{10}{20}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Thus $\lambda_2 = \lambda/\sqrt{2}$, confirming that option D is correct.

67398.subject: Physics
67398.text: Let $\gamma_1$ be the ratio of molar specific heat at constant pressure and molar specific heat at constant volume of a mono-atomic gas and $\gamma_2$ be the similar ratio of diatomic gas. Considering the diatomic gas molecule as a rigid rotator, the ratio, $\gamma_1 / \gamma_2$ is
67398.sol:
For a mono-atomic gas, the number of degrees of freedom is $f_1 = 3$.

The ratio of specific heats is $\gamma_1 = 1 + \dfrac{2}{f_1} = 1 + \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{5}{3}$.

For a diatomic gas acting as a rigid rotator, the number of degrees of freedom is $f_2 = 5$ (3 translational and 2 rotational).

The ratio of specific heats is $\gamma_2 = 1 + \dfrac{2}{f_2} = 1 + \dfrac{2}{5} = \dfrac{7}{5}$.

The required ratio is $\dfrac{\gamma_1}{\gamma_2} = \dfrac{5/3}{7/5} = \dfrac{25}{21}$.

Answer: $25/21$

67543.subject: Physics
67543.text: A particle describes a horizontal circle on smooth inner surface of a cone as shown in figure. If the height of the circle above the vertex is 10 cm. The speed of the particle is (g, acceleration due to gravity $=10 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ )
67543.sol:
A particle moves in uniform circular motion on the smooth inner surface of a cone. The vertical component of the normal force balances gravity, while the horizontal component provides centripetal force.

Resolving the normal force $N$ acting perpendicular to the surface: $N \cos\theta = mg$ vertically, and $N \sin\theta = mv^2/R$ horizontally. Eliminating $N$ gives $\tan\theta = v^2/(Rg)$.

From the cone's geometry, $\tan\theta = h/R$. Substituting yields:

$v^2 = Rg \cdot \frac{h}{R} = gh$

With $h = 0.1 \text{ m}$ and $g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$, we obtain:

$v^2 = (10)(0.1) = 1 \text{ m}^2/\text{s}^2$
$v = 1 \text{ m/s}$

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

68683.text: A mass $0.4$ kg performs S.H.M. with a frequency $\dfrac{16}{\pi}$ Hz. At a certain displacement it has kinetic energy $2$ J and potential energy $1.2$ J. The amplitude of oscillation is
68683.sol:
Total energy of the particle is the sum of kinetic and potential energy:

$E = K + U = 2 + 1.2 = 3.2$ J

The angular frequency of the simple harmonic motion is:

$\omega = 2\pi f = 2\pi \left(\dfrac{16}{\pi}\right) = 32$ rad/s

The total energy in SHM is given by:

$E = \dfrac{1}{2} m \omega^2 A^2$

Substituting the given values:

$3.2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 0.4 \times (32)^2 \times A^2$

$3.2 = 0.2 \times 1024 \times A^2$

$A^2 = \dfrac{3.2}{204.8} = \dfrac{1}{64}$

$A = \dfrac{1}{8} = 0.125$ m

Answer: $0.125$ m

68963.subject: Physics
68963.text: A glass cube of length 21 cm has a small air bubble trapped inside. When viewed normally from one face, its apparent distance is 8 cm. When viewed normally from the opposite face, its apparent distance is 6 cm. The refractive index of the glass and the actual distance of the air bubble from the first surface respectively are:
68963.sol:
The refractive index $n$ of the glass and the actual distance $d_1$ of the air bubble from the first face must be determined. The total thickness of the glass cube is $L = 21\text{ cm}$.

When viewed normally from the first face, the apparent distance is $8\text{ cm}$, giving the relation for apparent depth: $n = \frac{d_1}{8}$, so $d_1 = 8n$.

When viewed from the opposite face, the apparent distance is $6\text{ cm}$, and the actual distance from that face is $d_2 = 21 - d_1$. Using the apparent depth formula again: $n = \frac{21 - d_1}{6}$, so $21 - d_1 = 6n$.

Substituting $d_1 = 8n$ into this equation yields $21 - 8n = 6n$, resulting in $21 = 14n$ and $n = \frac{3}{2} = 1.5$.

Then $d_1 = 8 \times 1.5 = 12\text{ cm}$.

The correct option is A: $1.5, 12\text{ cm}$.

71489.subject: Biology
71489.text:
Match type of outbreeding device given in Column I with respective example given in Column II
Column (I)Column (II)
(A) Protogyny(I) Calotropis
(B) Herkogamy(II) Primula
(C) Self sterility(III) Gloriosa
(D) Heterostyly(IV) Thea
Choose the correct option
options: A - III, B - IV, C - II, D - I
A - III, B - I, C - II, D - IV
A - III, B - I, C - IV, D - II
A - II, B - III, C - IV, D - I
71489.sol:
Protogyny is a condition where the stigma matures earlier than the anthers, preventing self-pollination. An example is Gloriosa.

Herkogamy refers to the presence of a physical barrier between the anthers and stigma of the same flower, as seen in Calotropis.

Self sterility or self-incompatibility is a genetic mechanism that prevents self-pollen from fertilizing the ovules. An example is Thea.

Heterostyly is the presence of different lengths of styles and stamens in flowers of the same species, such as in Primula.

Thus, A matches with III, B matches with I, C matches with IV, and D matches with II.

Answer: A - III, B - I, C - IV, D - II

71855.subject: Chemistry
71855.text: Which one of the following alkenes forms the same product with HBr in the absence as well as in the presence of peroxide?
71855.sol:
Symmetrical alkenes yield the same product with HBr in the presence and absence of peroxide because both carbons of the double bond are equivalent.

2-butene (CH_3-CH=CH-CH_3$) is a symmetrical alkene.

Addition of HBr to 2-butene in the absence of peroxide (electrophilic addition) yields 2-bromobutane.

Addition of HBr to 2-butene in the presence of peroxide (free radical addition) also yields 2-bromobutane.

1-butene, propene, and 2-methylpropene are unsymmetrical alkenes and will yield different products (Markovnikov and anti-Markovnikov products) under these two conditions.

Answer: 2-butene$

71863.subject: Chemistry
71863.text: The degree of dissociation of weak acid is directly proportional to
options: volume of the solution containing $1$ mole of the weak acid
square of volume of the solution containing $1$ mole of the weak acid
square root of the volume containing $1$ mole of the weak acid
concentration of solution containing $1$ mole of the weak acid
71863.sol:
According to Ostwald's dilution law for a weak acid $HA$, the dissociation constant $K_a$ is given by:

$K_a = \dfrac{C\alpha^2}{1-\alpha}$

For a weak acid, the degree of dissociation $\alpha$ is very small ($\alpha \ll 1$), so $1-\alpha \approx 1$.

$K_a \approx C\alpha^2 \Rightarrow \alpha = \sqrt{\dfrac{K_a}{C}}$

The concentration $C$ is the number of moles per unit volume. For $1$ mole of the weak acid, $C = \dfrac{1}{V}$, where $V$ is the volume of the solution.

Substituting $C = \dfrac{1}{V}$ into the expression for $\alpha$:

$\alpha = \sqrt{K_a \times V}$

$\alpha \propto \sqrt{V}$

Thus, the degree of dissociation is directly proportional to the square root of the volume of the solution containing $1$ mole of the weak acid.

Answer: square root of the volume containing $1$ mole of the weak acid

72032.subject: Chemistry
72032.text: Which of the following statements regarding spontaneous process is NOT true?
options: It proceeds in both directions even in absence of external stimulant.
Spontaneity is not concerned with rate of reaction.
It continues till equilibrium is reached.
72032.sol:
A spontaneous process is one that occurs on its own without any external assistance.

It is a unidirectional process, meaning it proceeds only in one direction under a given set of conditions. It cannot proceed in the reverse direction without the help of an external agency. Therefore, it does not proceed in both directions.

Thermodynamics determines the spontaneity of a process but provides no information about the rate of the reaction (kinetics).

A spontaneous process continues until the system reaches a state of equilibrium.

Thus, the statement that it proceeds in both directions even in the absence of an external stimulant is incorrect.

Answer: It proceeds in both directions even in absence of external stimulant.

74127.text: Power of lens of focal length 25 cm is
74127.sol:
We define the power of a lens as the reciprocal of the focal length of the lens. So, the power of the lens is expressed as $\mathrm{P}=1 / \mathrm{f}$
Where $f$ is the focal length and is expressed in meters. So, the unit of power of the lens is expressed in $\mathrmm^{-1}$. This is also expressed as diopter.
As we know that the focal length of a convex lens is taken as in positive sign and the focal length of a concave lens is taken negatively. So, the power of a convex lens is positive, and the power of a concave lens is negative.
In this question, it is given that the lens is convex, and its focal length is 25 cm . First, we will convert the focal length into meters.
$\Rightarrow 25 \mathrm{ cm}=0.25 \mathrm{ m} \Rightarrow 25 \mathrm{ cm}=0.25 \mathrm{ m}$

80521.text: The viability of seeds is tested by:
80521.sol:
Viability of seeds can be known by two methods: (i) ability to germinate,
(ii) testing their ability to respire.
All viable seeds respire. This can be tested by immersing a section of seed containing the embryo in $0.1 \%$ solution of triphenyl tetrazolium chloride. The viable embryo will turn pink due to conversion of colourless triphenyl tetrazolium chloride into insoluble coloured dye called triphenyl formazone due to reduction. Tetrazolium Chloride (TZ) test is also called as quick germination test.
Related Theory
Seed or plant viability is the measure of how many seeds or how much plant material in a lot are alive and could develop into plants that will reproduce under appropriate field conditions. It is very important that seeds or plant material stored in the gene bank are capable of producing plants when sown in the field. They must have high viability at the start of storage and maintain it during storage, as it will stored for a longer period of time.

84065.subject: Zoology
84065.text: Which of the following is associated with decrease in cardiac output?
84065.sol:
The sympathetic nerve ending releases noradrenaline which stimulates the SAN that accelerates the heartbeat, the strength of ventricular contraction and thereby the cardiac output.

The parasympathetic nerve ending releases acetylcholine which decreases the rate of heartbeat, speed of conduction of action potential and thereby the cardiac output.

The adrenal medulla of the adrenal gland secretes two hormones called adrenaline and noradrenaline. Both the hormones are rapidly secreted in response to the stress of any kind and during emergency situations. These hormones increase the heartbeat and strength of heart contraction. Thus, adrenal medullary hormones can also increase cardiac output.

The pneumotaxic centre increases the rate of pulmonary ventilation, which in turn increases heartbeat and thus cardiac output.

85812.subject: Biology
85812.text:
Three different bacterial strains (P, Q, and R) when grown independently in a culture medium showed typical growth curves. Equal number of cells from all three actively growing cultures are mixed and grown together for $10$ days. The number of bacteria (N$) are counted each day and plotted.

Assuming nutrients are not limiting, the correct explanation for the observed trend is:$
options: P is an antibiotic producer, Q is antibiotic resistant, and R is antibiotic sensitive but evolves resistance during the course of the experiment.
Q is an antibiotic producer, P is antibiotic sensitive, and R is antibiotic sensitive but evolves resistance during the course of the experiment.
R is an antibiotic producer, P is antibiotic sensitive, and Q is antibiotic resistant.
Q is an antibiotic producer, P is antibiotic sensitive, and R is antibiotic resistant.
85812.sol:
Based on the growth curves of the mixed culture:

Strain $Q$ exhibits a normal logistic growth curve, reaching a plateau. This indicates it is unaffected by the other strains and is likely the producer of an inhibitory substance (antibiotic).

Strain $P$ grows initially but experiences a continuous decline after day $4$. This suggests it is sensitive to the accumulating antibiotic produced by $Q$.

Strain $R$ shows an initial growth, followed by a decline (indicating sensitivity), and then a subsequent recovery and growth phase after day $8$. This biphasic curve is characteristic of a strain that is initially sensitive but evolves or acquires antibiotic resistance during the culture period.

Thus, $Q$ is the antibiotic producer, $P$ is sensitive, and $R$ is initially sensitive but evolves resistance.

Answer: Q is an antibiotic producer, P is antibiotic sensitive, and R is antibiotic sensitive but evolves resistance during the course of the experiment.

86351.subject: Mathematics
86351.text:
For a complex number $z = x + iy$, where $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$, denote $\hat{z} = y + ix$.
The locus of $z$ satisfying $|z + \hat{z}| = |z - \hat{z}|$ in the complex plane is
options: union of the real axis and the imaginary axis
86351.sol:
Given $z = x + iy$ and $\hat{z} = y + ix$.

$z + \hat{z} = (x + y) + i(x + y)$

$|z + \hat{z}| = \sqrt{(x + y)^2 + (x + y)^2} = \sqrt{2}|x + y|$

$z - \hat{z} = (x - y) + i(y - x)$

$|z - \hat{z}| = \sqrt{(x - y)^2 + (y - x)^2} = \sqrt{2}|x - y|$

The given condition is $|z + \hat{z}| = |z - \hat{z}|$.

Substituting the magnitudes:

$\sqrt{2}|$x + y| = $\sqrt{2}|$x - y|$

Squaring both sides:

$(x + y)^2 = (x - y)^2$

$x^2 + y^2 + 2xy = x^2 + y^2 - 2xy$

4xy = 0 \Rightarrow xy = 0$

This implies $x = 0$ or $y = 0$.

$x = 0$ represents the imaginary axis and $y = 0$ represents the real axis.

Thus, the locus of $z$ is the union of the real axis and the imaginary axis.

92288.text: The number of solutions of the equation $lo{g}_{\sqrt{2}sin ⁡ x} ( 1 + cos ⁡ x ) = 2$ in the interval $\left[0, 5\pi\right]$ is
92288.sol:
${\log}_{\sqrt{2}sin ⁡ x}\left(1 + cos ⁡ x\right) = 2$
$1 + cos ⁡ x = {\left(\sqrt{2}sin ⁡ x\right)}^{2} = 2\sin^{2} ⁡ x$
$1 + cos ⁡ x = 2 - 2\cos^{2} ⁡ x$
$2\cos^{2} ⁡ x + cos ⁡ x - 1 = 0$
$⇒ \left(cos ⁡ x + 1\right)\left(2cos ⁡ x - 1\right) = 0$
$⇒ cos ⁡ x = \dfrac{1}{2}$ or cosx = - 1 (rejected)
$⇒ x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}, \dfrac{5\pi}{3} in \left[0,2\pi\right]$
But at $x = \dfrac{5\pi}{3}, \sqrt{2}sin ⁡ x$ is negative
$⇒ x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ in $\left[0,2\pi\right]$
$⇒ x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}, \dfrac{\pi}{3} + 2\pi, \dfrac{\pi}{3} + 4\pi$
$⇒ 3$ solutions in $\left[0, 5\pi\right]$

93138.text: Two spheres of electric charges $+ 2nC$ and $-8nC$ are placed at a distance $d$ apart. If they are allowed to touch each other, what is the new distance between them to get a repulsive force of same magnitude as before?
93138.sol:
In the first condition,

Given, ${q}_{1} = + 2nC = 2 \times {10}^{- 9}$

${q}_{2} = - 8 C$

$= - 8 \times {10}^{- 9} C$

$F = \dfrac{k{q}_{1}{q}_{2}}{{r}^{2}}$

$F = \dfrac{k\left(2 \times {10}^{- 9}\right) \times \left(8 \times {10}^{- 9}\right)}{{d}^{2}}$

$F = \dfrac{k\left(16 \times {10}^{- 18}\right)}{{d}^{2}}$ .....(i)

In the second condition,

${F}_{1} = \dfrac{k{q}_{1}{q}_{2}}{{d′}^{2}}$

After touching of sphere to each other the total charge $= 2 - 8 = - 6 nC$

charge on each sphere $= 3nC$

$= 3 \times {10}^{- 9}C$

${F}_{1} = \dfrac{k\left(3 \times {10}^{- 9}\right)\left(3 \times {10}^{- 9}\right)}{{\left({d}^{′}\right)}^{2}}$

${F}_{1} = \dfrac{k\left(9 \times {10}^{- 18}\right)}{{\left({d}^{′}\right)}^{2}}$ ...(ii)

From Equations. (i) and (ii), we get

$\dfrac{k\left(16 \times {10}^{- 18}\right)}{{d}^{2}} = \dfrac{k\left(9 \times {10}^{- 18}\right)}{{\left({d}^{′}\right)}^{2}}$

$\dfrac{{d}^{2}}{{d}^{′2}} = \dfrac{16 \times {10}^{- 18}}{9 \times {10}^{- 18}}$

$\dfrac{{d}^{2}}{{d}^{′2}} = \dfrac{16}{9}$

$\dfrac{d}{{d}^{′}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{16}{9}}$

$\dfrac{d}{{d}^{′}} = \dfrac{4}{3}$

$d = \dfrac{4}{3}{d}^{′}$

${d}^{′} = \dfrac{3}{4}d$

95892.subject: Botany
95892.text: CJD, black stem rust of wheat & potato spindle tuber disease are respectively caused by
options: viroid, tobacco mosaic virus, parasitic fungi
95892.sol:
The most notable diseases caused by prions are bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) commonly called mad cow disease in cattle and its analogous variant Cr–Jacob disease (CJD) in humans.
In 1971, T.O. Diener discovered a new infectious agent that was smaller than viruses and caused potato spindle tuber disease. It was found to be a free RNA; it lacked the protein coat that is found in viruses, hence the name viroid. The RNA of the viroid was of low molecular weight.
Some fungi cause diseases in plants and animals; wheat rust-causing Puccinia is an important example.& They grow in soil, on logs and tree stumps and in living plant bodies as parasites, e.g., rusts and smuts.

At physiological pH, the ammonia is protonated to form (ammonium) ion.

(i) Reductive amination : In these processes, ammonium ion reacts with α-ketoglutaric acid and forms glutamic acid. 98349.text: Malic acid inhibits the activity of enzyme succinate dehydrogenase. During this inhibition
98349.sol: Any substance that can diminish the velocity of an enzyme is known as an inhibitor. The two main types of inhibition are competitive, non-competitive. In competitive inhibition, the enzyme and inhibitor compete to bind to the same active site. Hence if substrate concentration is increased the chances of substrate binding to the enzyme will increase. Thus if (S) increases ${K}_{m}$ (Michaelis constant) also increases. In non-competitive inhibition, the substrate and inhibitor bind at different sites hence do not compete with each other. This cannot be reversed by increasing the substrate concentration and hence ${K}_{m}$ remains constant. This velocity of reaction also decreases. An example of a competitive inhibitor is malic acid. This competes with succinate (substrate) to bind at the active site of enzyme succinate dehydrogenase.

100013.subject: Physics
100013.text: A student measures human body temperature by placing a thermometer under the armpit. This method always gives a temperature reading that is lower than the actual internal body temperature. According to the classification of errors in measurement, this specific type of error is an example of:
100013.sol:
According to NCERT, measuring temperature under the armpit will always give a reading lower than the actual body temperature. This is a consistent error occurring in one direction due to a flawed procedure, which falls under the category of systematic errors, specifically termed as 'imperfection in experimental technique or procedure'.

It is not an instrumental error because the thermometer itself may be perfectly calibrated. It is not a personal error because it is not caused by individual carelessness or parallax. It is not a random error because the reading does not fluctuate unpredictably but is consistently lower.

Answer: Imperfection in experimental technique

101197.subject: Physics
101197.text: A uniform circular disc has original mass $M$ and radius $R$. A sector corresponding to an angle of $120^{\circ}$ is removed from it. The radius of gyration of the remaining part of the disc about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to its plane is:
101197.sol:
The mass of the remaining part of the disc is $m' = \dfrac{360^{\circ} - 120^{\circ}}{360^{\circ}} M = \dfrac{2}{3} M$.

The moment of inertia of a sector of a disc about its central axis is given by $I = \dfrac{1}{2} (\text{mass of sector}) R^2$.

Thus, the moment of inertia of the remaining part is $I' = \dfrac{1}{2} m' R^2$.

The radius of gyration $k$ is defined using the mass of the actual object, so $I' = m' k^2$.

Equating the two expressions for $I'$:
$m' k^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} m' R^2$

$k^2 = \dfrac{R^2}{2} \Rightarrow k = \dfrac{R}{\sqrt{2}}$.

Note that the radius of gyration of a sector of a uniform disc is independent of the angle of the sector and is the same as that of a complete disc.

Answer: $\dfrac{R}{\sqrt{2}}$

101664.subject: Physics
101664.text:
A horizontal venturimeter is used to measure the flow speed of water (density $= 1000 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$). The cross-sectional areas of the wide and narrow sections of the pipe are $30 \text{ cm}^2$ and $10 \text{ cm}^2$, respectively. A U-tube manometer connected between these two sections contains a liquid of density $5000 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$. If the height difference of the manometer liquid in the two arms is $40 \text{ cm}$, what is the flow speed of water at the wider section of the pipe?
[Take $g = 10 \text{ m s}^{-2}$]
101664.sol:
Let the flow speed at the wide section be $v_1$ and at the narrow section be $v_2$.

From the equation of continuity:

$A_1 v_1 = A_2 v_2$

$30 \times v_1 = 10 \times v_2 \Rightarrow v_2 = 3 v_1$

The pressure difference $\Delta P$ between the two sections is given by the manometer reading:

$\Delta P = (\rho_m - \rho_w) g h$

Substitute the given values ($\rho_m = 5000 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$, $\rho_w = 1000 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$, $h = 0.4 \text{ m}$):

$\Delta P = (5000 - 1000) \times 10 \times 0.4 = 4000 \times 4 = 16000 \text{ Pa}$

Applying Bernoulli's equation for a horizontal pipe:

$\Delta P = \dfrac{1}{2} \rho_w (v_2^2 - v_1^2)$

$16000 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1000 \times ((3 v_1)^2 - v_1^2)$

$16000 = 500 \times (9 v_1^2 - v_1^2)$

$16000 = 500 \times 8 v_1^2$

$16000 = 4000 v_1^2$

$v_1^2 = 4 \Rightarrow v_1 = 2 \text{ m s}^{-1}$

Answer: $2 \text{ m s}^{-1}$

101670.subject: Physics
101670.text: An air bubble of radius $2 \text{ mm}$ is rising at a steady speed of $2.5 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$ through a liquid column. If the coefficient of viscosity of the liquid is $0.5 \text{ kg m}^{-1} \text{ s}^{-1}$, what is the magnitude and direction of the viscous drag force acting on the bubble?
101670.sol:
Given:
Radius of the bubble, $r = 2 \text{ mm} = 2 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$
Steady velocity, $v = 2.5 \text{ cm s}^{-1} = 2.5 \times 10^{-2} \text{ m s}^{-1}$
Coefficient of viscosity, $\eta = 0.5 \text{ kg m}^{-1} \text{ s}^{-1}$

According to Stokes' law, the magnitude of the viscous drag force is:
$F = 6\pi\eta r v$
$F = 6\pi \times 0.5 \times (2 \times 10^{-3}) \times (2.5 \times 10^{-2})$
$F = 3\pi \times 5 \times 10^{-5}$
$F = 15\pi \times 10^{-5} \text{ N} = 1.5\pi \times 10^{-4} \text{ N}$

Viscous drag always opposes the relative motion of the object through the fluid. Since the air bubble is rising (moving vertically upwards), the viscous drag force must act vertically downwards.

Answer: $1.5\pi \times 10^{-4} \text{ N}$, vertically downwards

102233.subject: Physics
102233.text: Two ideal gases, helium and oxygen, are maintained in separate containers at identical temperature and pressure. The ratio of the mass density of helium to that of oxygen is:
102233.sol:
The ideal gas equation in terms of mass density $\rho$ is given by $P = \dfrac{\rho RT}{M_0}$, where $M_0$ is the molar mass of the gas.

Rearranging for density, we get $\rho = \dfrac{P M_0}{RT}$.

Since the pressure $P$ and temperature $T$ are identical for both gases, the mass density is directly proportional to the molar mass ($\rho \propto M_0$).

The molar mass of monatomic helium ($He$) is $4$ g/mol and the molar mass of diatomic oxygen ($O_2$) is $32$ g/mol.

The required ratio is $\dfrac{\rho_{He}}{\rho_{O_2}} = \dfrac{4}{32} = \dfrac{1}{8}$, which is $1 : 8$.

Using the atomic mass of oxygen ($16$ g/mol) instead of its molecular mass leads to the incorrect ratio $1 : 4$.

Answer: $1 : 8$

102882.subject: Physics
102882.text: The magnitude of the electric field $E$ of a spherically symmetric charge distribution varies with the distance $r$ from its centre. The graph of $E$ versus $r$ shows that $E$ increases linearly from zero at $r=0$ to a maximum value $E_0$ at $r=R$, and then decreases for $r > R$. A point charge $q$ is moved slowly from the centre ($r=0$) to the surface ($r=R$) along a random curved path. What is the magnitude of the work done by the external agent in this process?
102882.sol:
The electrostatic field is conservative, meaning the work done in moving a charge is independent of the path taken and depends only on the initial and final positions.

The work done by an external agent in moving a charge $q$ slowly is given by $W = q \Delta V$, where $\Delta V$ is the potential difference between the final and initial points.

The magnitude of the potential difference $|\Delta V|$ between $r=0$ and $r=R$ is equal to the magnitude of the line integral of the electric field, which corresponds to the area under the $E$ versus $r$ graph from $r=0$ to $r=R$.

Since the graph of $E$ versus $r$ is linear from $0$ to $E_0$ over the distance $R$, the region forms a right-angled triangle with base $R$ and height $E_0$.

Area under the curve = $\dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \dfrac{1}{2} R E_0$

Thus, the magnitude of the potential difference is $|\Delta V| = \dfrac{1}{2} R E_0$.

The magnitude of the work done by the external agent is:
$|W| = q |\Delta V| = q \left( \dfrac{1}{2} R E_0 \right) = \dfrac{q R E_0}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{q R E_0}{2}$

103131.text: Three identical capacitors $C_1$, $C_2$ and $C_3$, each of capacitance $C$, are connected to a DC source of voltage $V$. Capacitors $C_1$ and $C_2$ are connected in parallel, and their combination is connected in series with $C_3$. What is the ratio of the energy stored in capacitor $C_1$ to the energy stored in capacitor $C_3$?
103131.sol:
The equivalent capacitance of the parallel combination of $C_1$ and $C_2$ is:
$C_{12} = C + C = 2C$

This combination is connected in series with $C_3$ (capacitance $C$) across the voltage source $V$. In a series circuit, the voltage divides inversely as the capacitance. The voltage across the parallel combination (which is the voltage across $C_1$) is:
$V_1 = V \times \dfrac{C_3}{C_{12} + C_3} = V \times \dfrac{C}{2C + C} = \dfrac{V}{3}$

The voltage across $C_3$ is:
$V_3 = V \times \dfrac{C_{12}}{C_{12} + C_3} = V \times \dfrac{2C}{2C + C} = \dfrac{2V}{3}$

The energy stored in capacitor $C_1$ is:
$U_1 = \dfrac{1}{2} C_1 V_1^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} C \left(\dfrac{V}{3}\right)^2 = \dfrac{CV^2}{18}$

The energy stored in capacitor $C_3$ is:
$U_3 = \dfrac{1}{2} C_3 V_3^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} C \left(\dfrac{2V}{3}\right)^2 = \dfrac{4CV^2}{18}$

The ratio of the energy stored in $C_1$ to that in $C_3$ is:
$\dfrac{U_1}{U_3} = \dfrac{\dfrac{CV^2}{18}}{\dfrac{4CV^2}{18}} = \dfrac{1}{4}$

Answer: $1:4$
